question: What is a primary benefit of addressing workplace conflicts early in a clinical setting?

options.A: It prevents small disagreements from turning into a toxic atmosphere
options.B: It removes the need for shift handovers and team meetings
options.C: It stops doctors from ever questioning nursing care plans
options.D: It guarantees that nurses receive an immediate salary increase

explanation: Correct! Addressing issues early keeps the ward vibe positive and ensures patient safety stays front and center. [learn more](GST321_U7_T2#GST321_U7_T2_h7)

question: What role does the involucrum play in chronic bone infection?

options.A: It is the primary channel through which bacteria enter the bloodstream
options.B: It is a soft tissue tumor that mimics bone cancer on an X-ray
options.C: It acts as a sponge that absorbs antibiotics and neutralizes them
options.D: It is new bone formed by the periosteum to wall off the dead bone

explanation: The body creates an outer shell of living new bone called an involucrum around the dead bone segment during the chronic phase. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h3)

question: A patient has a stroke affecting the left frontal lobe. As a nurse, what sign might you notice?

options.A: Total loss of hearing in both ears
options.B: Complete blindness in the left eye
options.C: Difficulty with voluntary movement on the right side
options.D: Inability to recognize familiar faces

explanation: The frontal lobe handles movement. Because brain pathways cross over, the left side of your brain controls the right side of your body! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h3)

question: A conscious patient's random blood sugar is 52 mg/dL and they feel shaky. What should you do right away?

options.A: Give 15 grams of fast-acting oral carbohydrates
options.B: Send the patient for an emergency CT scan of the head
options.C: Inject long-acting insulin into the deltoid muscle
options.D: Wait patiently for two hours and test the blood again

explanation: Since the patient is awake and able to swallow, give them quick-acting sugar (like glucose tablets or juice) to bring their blood sugar back up safely. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T19#GNS222_U2_T19_h7)

question: What causes the initial change in charge when an action potential starts in a neuron?

options.A: Potassium ions leave the cell permanently
options.B: Calcium ions are stored in the nucleus
options.C: Sodium ions rush into the cell
options.D: Neurotransmitters dissolve the cell membrane

explanation: The opening of sodium channels allows positive sodium ions to flood inward, reversing the membrane charge. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h6)

question: Which mental health issue is most commonly diagnosed in survivors of severe violence?

options.A: Bipolar mood disorder
options.B: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD)
options.C: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
options.D: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD)

explanation: Correct! Survivors of intense physical, emotional, or sexual trauma very often develop PTSD because of the deep impact of their experience. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T14#GNS313_U3_T14_h4)

question: Why is the involvement of religious and traditional leaders crucial for eliminating harmful practices?

options.A: They control the primary budgets for hospital construction
options.B: They possess formal medical licenses to treat surgical complications
options.C: They hold significant moral authority and influence community behavior
options.D: They are legally mandated to act as local health inspectors

explanation: Community members listen closely to religious and traditional elders, making their support vital for shifting cultural norms. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h4)

question: In nursing, what does the term 'polypharmacy' mean?

options.A: Using a machine to deliver intravenous fluids
options.B: Taking multiple medications at the same time
options.C: Receiving treatment in a private hospital room
options.D: Having a severe allergy to common antibiotics

explanation: Polypharmacy simply means taking many drugs at once. This often increases the risk of side effects and drug clashes, so nurses have to monitor these patients closely. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T8#GNS122_U3_T8_h3)

question: How does untreated cervicitis affect a patient's risk of contracting HIV?

options.A: It grants temporary immunity against sexually transmitted viruses.
options.B: It decreases the risk because white blood cells destroy the virus.
options.C: It increases the risk because the mucosal tissue is broken and immune cells are rushed to the area.
options.D: It has no measurable impact on viral transmission rates.

explanation: Inflamed, fragile tissue plus a gathering of immune cells gives viruses like HIV an easier pathway into the body. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h7)

question: A patient in strict isolation cries because no one wants to touch them without gear. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Assure them that the infection is not serious at all
options.B: Remove your gown and gloves to prove you care
options.C: Tell them the rules are necessary and leave the room quickly
options.D: Acknowledge their feelings and spend time talking calmly with them

explanation: Validating emotions and offering supportive conversation helps reduce the psychological toll of isolation while keeping safety intact. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h7)

question: What happens if you manage to disrupt just one single link in the chain of infection?

options.A: The pathogen automatically changes into a harmless virus
options.B: The susceptible host becomes permanently immune
options.C: The infection process is completely stopped
options.D: The reservoir doubles its reproductive rate

explanation: Brilliant! The chain needs every single link to stay connected. Break just one, and the disease is stopped in its tracks. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T9#GNS324_U6_T9_h2)

question: A patient asks why her doctor checked estriol levels specifically during her pregnancy. What is the main source of estriol?

options.A: The anterior pituitary
options.B: The placenta
options.C: The thyroid gland
options.D: The adrenal medulla

explanation: The placenta pumps out loads of estriol during pregnancy. Doctors use it as a helpful check to see how well the baby and placenta are doing! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T6#GNS121_U5_T6_h2)

question: What is a major safety concern when giving sleeping pills (sedative-hypnotics) to older adults?

options.A: Severe respiratory alkalosis
options.B: Hypertensive crisis
options.C: Permanent hearing loss
options.D: Increased risk of falls

explanation: Sleeping pills can cause daytime drowsiness and dizziness, making older adults unsteady on their feet and putting them at a high risk for accidental falls. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T12#GNS123_U3_T12_h7)

question: Which lab values must a nurse check before a patient receives gadolinium contrast dye for an MRI?

options.A: Fasting blood glucose and hemoglobin A1c
options.B: Kidney function tests like creatinine and BUN
options.C: Liver enzymes and total protein counts
options.D: Complete blood count and platelet levels

explanation: Contrast dye is filtered through the kidneys, so poor kidney function can lead to dangerous complications like nephrogenic systemic fibrosis. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h5)

question: Why do your glands (lymph nodes) often swell up and feel tender when you have an infection?

options.A: The flow of lymph fluid has stopped completely due to local blockage
options.B: White blood cells are rapidly multiplying inside them to fight the invader
options.C: Red blood cells are accumulating in the tissue to repair damaged vessels
options.D: The local temperature has dropped below normal physiological levels

explanation: You got it! When germs are around, your white blood cells throw a massive training and multiplying party inside the nodes, making them temporarily swollen and tender. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T2#GNS123_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why does ongoing urinary incontinence put a patient at higher risk for urinary tract infections?

options.A: Skin breakdown allows bacteria to travel directly into the bloodstream
options.B: Frequent urination washes away all the normal protective cells
options.C: Moisture and residual urine create an environment where bacteria multiply easily
options.D: Absorbent pads permanently stop the kidneys from filtering waste

explanation: Sticking around in lingering moisture gives bacteria a cozy place to grow and easily find their way into the urinary tract. Good skin care and hygiene prevent this! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h8)

question: How can hormonal shifts and physical stress impact a patient who already has a mental health condition?

options.A: They can significantly worsen existing psychiatric disorders
options.B: They permanently cure depression and anxiety
options.C: They have no impact on emotional well-being
options.D: They only affect physical organ function

explanation: Recovering from physical stress combined with sudden hormone changes can easily trigger or intensify existing mental health challenges. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h5)

question: How is primary nursing different from traditional task-oriented nursing?

options.A: Task-oriented nursing focuses on splitting chores among staff, whereas primary nursing focuses on holistic, continuous care by one nurse.
options.B: Task-oriented nursing eliminates the need for registered nurses on the hospital floor entirely.
options.C: Primary nursing relies solely on unlicensed assistive personnel for all bedside duties.
options.D: Task-oriented nursing requires patients to change their assigned nurse every single hour.

explanation: Think of task nursing like a factory assembly line where everyone does one chore (like just giving injections), while primary nursing gives one nurse the full picture of the patient's wellbeing. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T3#GNS123_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why is having a written emergency plan important for families with vulnerable members?

options.A: It is required by law for every residential building
options.B: It lowers the monthly cost of utility bills
options.C: It stops equipment from breaking during storms
options.D: It prevents panic and guides quick action during a crisis

explanation: When an emergency happens, stress is high, so having clear steps written down helps everyone respond calmly and correctly. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h8)

question: Why must a patient return 48 to 72 hours after getting a Mantoux injection?

options.A: To ensure the PPD liquid does not leak out of the skin layers
options.B: To receive a second booster dose in the exact same location
options.C: To allow enough time for the delayed immune reaction to peak
options.D: To prevent the injection site from becoming infected with bacteria

explanation: The cellular immune response takes two to three days to build enough local induration to be accurately measured by a healthcare provider. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h2)

question: What is the immediate first-aid step after sustaining an accidental needle-stick injury?

options.A: Squeeze the puncture wound hard to force blood out
options.B: Soak the affected finger in undiluted bleach
options.C: Wash the site thoroughly with soap and running water
options.D: Apply a strong iodine solution and cover it tightly

explanation: Washing with soap and water immediately helps remove contaminants before they enter the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h6)

question: Which common anti-TB drug is famous for turning urine and tears a harmless red-orange color?

options.A: Ethambutol
options.B: Isoniazid
options.C: Pyrazinamide
options.D: Rifampicin

explanation: Rifampicin gives body fluids a reddish tint. As a nurse, warning your patients about this beforehand saves them a lot of panic! [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h2)

question: As a nurse, what is a crucial warning sign of an ectopic pregnancy you must teach patients to report right away?

options.A: Mild generalized fatigue and mild morning nausea
options.B: Temporary swelling in the lower extremities
options.C: Clear and painless watery vaginal discharge
options.D: One-sided sharp pelvic pain with abnormal spotting

explanation: Sharp pain on just one side of the lower belly, paired with unusual bleeding, is a major red flag for an ectopic pregnancy that needs urgent care. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T26#GNS216_U5_T26_h8)

question: A lab report describes tissue with disordered growth and cells of varying shapes and sizes. Which term describes this?

options.A: Metaplasia
options.B: Dysplasia
options.C: Hyperplasia
options.D: Atrophy

explanation: Well done! Dysplasia means disordered growth where cells lose their normal shape and organization—often an early warning sign that nurses watch closely. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h2)

question: A patient with advanced dementia makes a pain face, holds their tummy, and has a fast heart rate, but says they have no pain. What should you do?

options.A: Discharge the patient because they cannot feel pain.
options.B: Ignore the physical signs since the verbal denial overrides them.
options.C: Treat these non-verbal behavioral signs as reliable indicators of pain.
options.D: Wait until the patient is able to provide a clear numeric score.

explanation: When dementia makes talking difficult, body language tells the real story. Trust those physical cues! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T5#GNS321_U4_T5_h5)

question: Which of these tasks is safe and appropriate to hand over (delegate) to assistive personnel?

options.A: Administering intravenous pain medication for acute trauma
options.B: Creating the initial nursing care plan for a new admission
options.C: Taking routine vital signs for a stable postoperative patient
options.D: Evaluating the healing progress of a surgical incision

explanation: Spot on! Stable patients and routine vitals are great for assistive staff, freeing you up to handle the more complex clinical duties. [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h5)

question: Which of the following is a good practice, and NOT a common mistake in research proposals?

options.A: Failing to plan proper ethical protections
options.B: Choosing a topic that is far too broad to manage
options.C: Relying heavily on outdated reference materials
options.D: Ensuring alignment between questions and methods

explanation: Making sure your research questions match your methods is a brilliant practice! The other options are classic pitfalls to avoid. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T1#GNS224_U3_T1_h8)

question: What tool do managers commonly use to track progress toward objectives?

options.A: Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
options.B: Random patient complaint letters
options.C: Daily weather forecasts
options.D: Personal diary entries

explanation: KPIs provide measurable data that helps managers track whether goals are being met. [learn more](GST321_U2_T3#GST321_U2_T3_h7)

question: What kind of stool do you usually see when someone has bleeding in their upper gut (like the stomach)?

options.A: Bright red streaks on the surface
options.B: Pale, clay-colored, bulky stools
options.C: Dark, tarry stools known as melena
options.D: Hard, dry, pellet-like stools

explanation: When blood travels all the way from the upper digestive tract, digestive juices break it down and turn it dark and sticky like tar by the time it comes out. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T2#GNS213_U3_T2_h2)

question: Why is it super helpful for nurses to understand basic X-ray imaging?

options.A: To replace the radiologist in reading films
options.B: To prescribe the correct radiation dosage
options.C: To operate the heavy X-ray machine safely
options.D: To help coordinate care and ease patient anxiety

explanation: As a nurse, you are the friendly face who prepares patients and calms their nerves before procedures. Great nursing starts with great communication! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h1)

question: Which layer of the meninges is the tough, outermost layer attached to the skull?

options.A: Choroid plexus
options.B: Arachnoid mater
options.C: Dura mater
options.D: Pia mater

explanation: The dura mater is a thick, durable membrane providing sturdy outer protection for the brain and spinal cord. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h7)

question: What is the main difference between curative care and palliative care?

options.A: Palliative care is only used in hospitals, while curative is at home
options.B: Curative care ignores pain, while palliative care uses surgery
options.C: Curative aims to cure disease, while palliative aims to relieve suffering
options.D: Palliative care is only for children, while curative is for adults

explanation: You've got this! Curative care fights to get rid of the illness, while palliative care focuses on making sure the patient is comfortable and free from heavy suffering. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T2#GNS321_U4_T2_h3)

question: How is segmentation different from peristalsis in the gut?

options.A: Segmentation occurs only in the stomach while peristalsis is in the colon.
options.B: Segmentation mixes food back and forth rather than moving it forward.
options.C: Segmentation is controlled by the brain while peristalsis is automatic.
options.D: Segmentation stops all digestion while peristalsis speeds it up.

explanation: You're doing great! While peristalsis pushes food forward, segmentation uses ring-like squeezes to thoroughly blend food back and forth with digestive juices. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h7)

question: What name did Casimir Funk originally give to essential food factors that he believed were life-giving amines?

options.A: Macronutrients
options.B: Electrolytes
options.C: Vitamines
options.D: Caloric units

explanation: That's correct! He combined 'vital' and 'amines' to coin the term 'vitamines' for these crucial health-boosting substances. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T002#GNS227_U1_T002_h4)

question: What happens to C3 complement protein levels in the blood during active Post-Streptococcal Glomerulonephritis?

options.A: They rise to very high levels
options.B: They fluctuate every few hours
options.C: They drop below normal levels
options.D: They remain completely unchanged

explanation: Think of C3 proteins as defense workers that get completely used up and depleted by the ongoing immune battle in the kidneys, leaving low levels in the blood test. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T4#GNS213_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why is leaving an EMR workstation logged in and walk away a big professional risk?

options.A: Hospital management will automatically dock your monthly salary
options.B: Patients will be able to alter their own discharge instructions
options.C: Anyone can document care under your name, making you legally responsible
options.D: The computer screen saver will permanently burn out from inactivity

explanation: Always lock your screen! Because entries are tied to your specific login, you take the blame for anything done on that open terminal. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T9#GNS212_U4_T9_h6)

question: What is the primary function of an enteric coating on a tablet?

options.A: To resist stomach acid and dissolve in the intestine
options.B: To speed up absorption directly in the stomach
options.C: To allow the pill to be easily crushed into powder
options.D: To make the pill taste sweet for children

explanation: Enteric coatings protect drugs from stomach acid and protect the stomach lining from harsh medications by dissolving further down in the gut. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h2)

question: How do hydrogen ions help create a sour taste in the mouth?

options.A: By blocking potassium channels and lowering intracellular pH
options.B: By activating cyclic AMP inside the taste receptor cell
options.C: By binding to G-protein coupled receptors on Type II cells
options.D: By actively pumping chloride ions out of the taste pore

explanation: When hydrogen ions enter sour-sensing cells, they block potassium channels and drop the internal pH, triggering the cell to release signals. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T10#GNS211_U4_T10_h4)

question: Why do certain smells instantly trigger strong memories or emotions?

options.A: Smell signals pass through the visual cortex first
options.B: The nose shares a direct blood supply with the hippocampus
options.C: Odorants directly stimulate the motor strip in the frontal lobe
options.D: Olfactory pathways connect directly to the limbic system in the brain

explanation: You got it! Unlike other senses, smell signals bypass the brain's relay station (the thalamus) and go straight to emotional centers like the amygdala and hippocampus. That's why a scent can instantly remind you of home! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T9#GNS211_U4_T9_h1)

question: Why is simply giving out health information usually not enough to change community habits?

options.A: Knowledge does not automatically change daily practices
options.B: Communities prefer traditional medicine over clinics
options.C: People usually forget instructions given by nurses
options.D: Health messages are always too complex for villagers

explanation: Knowing what to do is a great first step, but real life has social and money hurdles that make acting on that knowledge tough. That's why community nursing is so hands-on! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T27#GNS225_U2_T27_h1)

question: What is the main consequence of damaged intestinal villi on a patient's nutrition?

options.A: The liver stops making bile needed for breaking down sugars.
options.B: The stomach starts producing too much acid for digestion.
options.C: Reduced surface area leads to poor absorption of essential nutrients.
options.D: Food moves backward into the esophagus causing frequent vomiting.

explanation: Intestinal villi are responsible for absorbing digested nutrients into the bloodstream; when they are damaged, nutrient uptake fails. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h4)

question: What is the recommended minimum birth spacing interval to protect maternal and child health?

options.A: One year apart
options.B: Exactly five years apart
options.C: Six months apart
options.D: Two to three years apart

explanation: Waiting two to three years between pregnancies allows the mother's body to recover fully and reduces risks for the newborn. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h1)

question: When do patients most commonly move into a skilled nursing facility?

options.A: When they want to change their primary care physician
options.B: Immediately following a hospital stay for acute illness or surgery
options.C: Right after receiving a routine annual checkup from a family doctor
options.D: Before an elective outpatient procedure scheduled next month

explanation: Most patients step down from the hospital to an SNF when they still need professional nursing care before heading back home. Great clinical insight! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h1)

question: How can community leaders help improve low immunization uptake in rural areas?

options.A: By importing vaccines directly from international manufacturers
options.B: By taking over clinical duties and injecting vaccines themselves
options.C: By replacing the cold chain refrigerators with local coolers
options.D: By building trust and addressing local rumors or hesitancy

explanation: Local chiefs and religious leaders have powerful voices. When they support immunization, community members feel much more confident bringing their babies in. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h6)

question: Oh no! A nurse gets a needle stick injury while dealing with a full sharps box. What is the very first thing she should do?

options.A: Wash the puncture site thoroughly with soap and running water
options.B: Complete an incident report form before washing the wound
options.C: Squeeze the puncture site hard to force out old blood
options.D: Apply a tight tourniquet above the elbow immediately

explanation: You've got it! Immediate washing with soap and running water helps wash away germs right away before you report the incident. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h7)

question: What is a major consequence of gender-based power imbalances in many communities?

options.A: Reduced autonomy for women regarding their health and reproductive decisions
options.B: Elimination of all barriers preventing men from accessing mental healthcare
options.C: Universal access to high-quality healthcare for gender-diverse people
options.D: Equal distribution of household resources among all family members

explanation: When power is concentrated unequally, women often lack the decision-making power needed to protect their own health and well-being. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h7)

question: Why do we prefer tube feeding (enteral nutrition) over drip feeding into a vein (parenteral nutrition) if the gut is working?

options.A: It lets the patient eat regular meals at the same time
options.B: It is much cheaper and needs no equipment
options.C: It has zero risk of infection
options.D: It keeps the gut lining healthy and prevents it from wasting away

explanation: Use it or lose it! Keeping food moving through the GI tract keeps the intestinal walls strong and stops bad bacteria from leaking out. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h3)

question: A patient is prescribed an inhaled bronchodilator and an inhaled corticosteroid. In what order should they take them?

options.A: Corticosteroid in the morning and bronchodilator only at bedtime
options.B: Both medications mixed together in the nebulizer at the same time
options.C: Corticosteroid first, wait a few minutes, then the bronchodilator
options.D: Bronchodilator first, wait a few minutes, then the corticosteroid

explanation: Open the door first! Taking the bronchodilator opens up the airways so the steroid that follows can travel much deeper into the lungs to fight inflammation. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T2#GNS223_U2_T2_h7)

question: Why do nurses encourage new mothers to walk around soon after delivery (early ambulation)?

options.A: To completely eliminate white blood cells from circulation
options.B: To stimulate the kidneys to stop producing erythropoietin
options.C: To help prevent dangerous blood clots in the deep veins
options.D: To immediately restore the pre-pregnancy plasma volume

explanation: Get those legs moving! Walking helps blood circulate properly and stops clots from forming in the legs after birth. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T1#GNS121_U7_T1_h7)

question: What happens when a person suffers severe damage to their hippocampus?

options.A: They lose the ability to feel physical pain
options.B: They experience paralysis in their lower limbs
options.C: They forget all their childhood memories
options.D: They can no longer form new long-term memories

explanation: You nailed it! The hippocampus is needed to lock in new experiences into long-term storage, so damage makes forming new memories very difficult. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T13#GNS211_U3_T13_h4)

question: What major nutrition challenges do dietitians frequently tackle in Nigeria?

options.A: Rare genetic disorders affecting bone density in infants
options.B: Protein-energy malnutrition and chronic lifestyle diseases
options.C: Severe vitamin toxicity from over-supplementation
options.D: High rates of scurvy among coastal fishing communities

explanation: Well done! Nigeria faces a double burden—dealing with undernutrition issues like kwashiorkor while also seeing a rise in lifestyle conditions like hypertension and diabetes. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T002#GNS227_U4_T002_h6)

question: Where is the safest place to give a vitamin K injection to a full-term newborn?

options.A: Ventral gluteal muscle
options.B: Vastus lateralis muscle
options.C: Deltoid muscle of the arm
options.D: Dorsogluteal muscle

explanation: The vastus lateralis in the outer thigh is the go-to spot! It's well-developed in newborns and keeps them safe from major nerves and blood vessels. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h5)

question: Which health worker is best at helping a patient relearn daily tasks like bathing, dressing, and cooking?

options.A: Occupational therapist
options.B: Pharmacist
options.C: Physiotherapist
options.D: Speech pathologist

explanation: Great job! Occupational therapists focus heavily on everyday living activities and finding smart ways to adapt tasks so the patient can manage on their own. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T17#GNS225_U5_T17_h3)

question: Why do fat-soluble (lipid-soluble) drugs cross cell membranes much easier than water-soluble ones?

options.A: Cell membranes are made of a lipid bilayer.
options.B: Fat-soluble drugs refuse to dissolve in body fluids.
options.C: Water-soluble drugs require active ATP energy pumps.
options.D: Lipid drugs are always smaller in molecular weight.

explanation: Like dissolves like! Since cell membranes are made of fat (lipids), fat-soluble drugs slip right through them easily. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T1#GNS125_U5_T1_h4)

question: Which simple tool does a healthcare provider use to actually see a cervical polyp?

options.A: Stethoscope
options.B: Otoscope
options.C: Speculum
options.D: Sphygmomanometer

explanation: A speculum gently opens the vaginal canal so the doctor can get a clear, direct look at the cervix. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h4)

question: Which of these conditions is a classic reason to use a Nelson inhaler?

options.A: Acute sinusitis
options.B: Bacterial pneumonia
options.C: Spontaneous pneumothorax
options.D: Pulmonary edema

explanation: Spot on! Sinusitis brings painful inflammation and blocked nasal passages, which respond wonderfully to the warm, soothing moisture of steam therapy. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T6#GNS212_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of nursing interventions in family-centered care?

options.A: To make all healthcare decisions on behalf of the household head
options.B: To strengthen the family's ability to care for its members independently
options.C: To permanently remove sick family members into institutions
options.D: To eliminate the need for doctors

explanation: Good nursing support empowers families so they gain confidence to manage their health challenges over time. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h7)

question: External rotation of the baby's head is actually caused by the turning of which body part?

options.A: The shoulders
options.B: The feet
options.C: The hips
options.D: The chest

explanation: Exactly! As the baby's shoulders twist inside to fit the pelvis, that movement travels up the neck and makes the head turn on the outside. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h6)

question: What is the main reason a patient experiences angina pectoris (chest pain)?

options.A: Inadequate oxygen supply to the heart muscle
options.B: Sudden electrical failure of the heart ventricles
options.C: Severe inflammation of the outer heart lining

question: How soon can ovulation return after an abortion procedure?

question: How does a Root Cause Analysis differ from simply blaming an individual worker?

question: An HIV-positive patient feels completely fine for eight years without taking meds. What stage is this?

question: Why do nurses sometimes use alternative checks like arm span or knee height for elderly patients instead of a standing height?

question: Which nervous system response directly triggers a penile erection?

question: What is polypharmacy, a common concern in care home residents?

question: What is the main purpose of the initial evaluation phase in rehabilitation?

question: If a patient has joint pain along with skin rashes and unusual sensitivity to sunlight, what systemic condition might they have?

question: What is the primary benefit of empowering parents in home healthcare?

question: Which hormone is released by special cells in the heart when the heart walls get stretched too much?

question: Why do patients with severe burns or major infections need significantly more calories than usual?

question: Why must an effective screening program have accessible treatment available?

question: What is a common physical risk of giving artificial IV hydration to a terminal patient?

question: What is the main goal of rehabilitation for patients with sensory organ disorders?

question: Which question is best when a nurse wants to understand how a patient is coping with their sickness?

options.C: What is your exact weight in kilograms today?

question: How many hours of fasting are typically required before a standard GTT begins?

question: Why must the packaging used for steam sterilization be porous (able to let air and steam through)?

options.A: To ensure the wrapper dissolves completely inside the machine

options.C: To let air escape so the package smells fresh when opened

question: What is the very first thing you should do before putting any topical medication on a patient's skin?

options.A: Massage the skin vigorously to increase blood flow
options.B: Apply a thick layer of petroleum jelly to protect surrounding tissue
options.C: Warm the cream under hot running water

question: If a patient suddenly cannot move their leg due to a spinal injury, which part of the spinal grey matter is likely damaged?

options.A: Dorsal horn
options.B: Lateral horn
options.C: Central canal
options.D: Ventral horn

question: Why can untreated vaginal infections sometimes lead to fertility problems?

options.C: Inflammation triggers the immediate closure of the vaginal canal.

question: While helping a patient walk, you notice their urine bag is hanging higher than their bladder. Why is this a problem?

options.A: Urine can flow backward into the bladder and cause an infection
options.B: The urine output will instantly turn bright red with blood
options.C: The plastic collection tubing will melt from body heat

question: If your rural clinic runs out of official safety boxes, what is a safe, clever backup plan for used needles?

options.A: Using locally available, puncture-resistant rigid containers
options.B: Throwing loose needles directly into the regular dustbin
options.C: Burying uncapped needles in the hospital garden
options.D: Washing and reusing disposable needles for multiple patients

question: If a patient has their entire pituitary gland surgically removed, which of these medications do they NOT need to take for the rest of their life?

options.A: Thyroid hormone replacement
options.B: Sex hormone replacement
options.C: Cortisol replacement (glucocorticoids)
options.D: Insulin injections

question: What is the primary focus of organisational objectives in healthcare?

options.A: The private business ventures of senior medical doctors
options.B: The daily social events organised by the nursing union
options.C: The personal retirement plans of individual staff members
options.D: The survival, growth, and overall service delivery of the institution

explanation: Organzational objectives look at the big picture—keeping the hospital running smoothly, growing, and providing great care to the community. [learn more](GST321_U2_T2#GST321_U2_T2_h3)

question: A client with asthma is wheezing heavily during an acute attack. What is the primary physical reason for this sound?

options.C: Air passing through narrowed, constricted airways

question: What makes electrical and chemical burns so tricky compared to normal flame burns?

options.A: They heal completely within twenty-four hours without scarring
options.B: They only affect the outermost layer of the dead skin cells
options.C: They never require immediate medical attention or hospital care
options.D: They frequently cause hidden internal tissue damage beneath the skin

explanation: Spot on! Electricity and chemicals can travel deep inside the body, meaning the damage under the skin is often much worse than what you see on the surface. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h3)

question: Where should the surgical needle be grasped by the needle holder?

options.A: At the extreme tail end of the thread

options.D: Directly in the exact middle of the curve

question: What trouble might a nurse administrator face by ignoring civil service rules and health laws?

options.A: Patients experience faster recovery times due to flexible management

options.C: The hospital automatically receives more funding from the federal budget

question: Why might a newly diagnosed patient temporarily use the defense mechanism of denial?

options.A: To protect the mind from overwhelming emotional pain
options.B: To increase their physical strength and immunity
options.C: To speed up cellular regeneration and wound healing
options.D: To permanently cure their underlying medical condition

explanation: Defense mechanisms like denial act as psychological buffers, shielding the individual from sudden, unbearable emotional shocks. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T6#GNS123_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why is family planning considered a key pillar of safe motherhood?

options.A: It helps women space pregnancies to protect their physical health
options.B: It eliminates the need for any laboratory tests during pregnancy
options.C: It completely stops women from experiencing menopause
options.D: It guarantees that every baby born will be a male child

explanation: Giving mum's body time to rest and rebuild strength between babies means a healthier mother and a safer next pregnancy! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T001#GNS226_U1_T001_h3)

question: Out of these options, which patient situation should a critical care nurse tackle FIRST?

options.A: Dry lips from breathing through an oxygen mask
options.B: Sudden drop in blood pressure with cold, pale skin
options.C: Mild anxiety about upcoming laboratory tests
options.D: Boredom due to lack of television entertainment

question: Which strategy helps a nurse prevent burnout when dealing with frequent patient losses?

options.A: Suppressing all feelings of sadness so nobody notices
options.B: Avoiding all patients who have terminal diagnoses
options.C: Participating in regular team debriefings and setting emotional boundaries
options.D: Working extra double shifts to stay distracted

explanation: Talking through tough losses with colleagues and keeping healthy boundaries protects your mental health and keeps your caring spirit strong! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T10#GNS321_U4_T10_h8)

question: Which of these symptoms should you teach a pregnant woman to report immediately as a danger sign?

options.A: Vaginal bleeding at any stage of pregnancy
options.B: Increased frequency of urination in the third trimester
options.C: Mild swelling of the ankles at the end of the day
options.D: Occasional mild heartburn after eating heavy meals

explanation: Vaginal bleeding is never normal during pregnancy and can point to serious issues like placenta previa or a miscarriage. Teaching mothers these danger signs saves lives! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T015#GNS226_U1_T015_h7)

question: A patient wants an IUD right after an uncomplicated surgical abortion. What is the standard clinical practice?

options.A: She must wait for two normal menstrual periods
options.B: It can be safely inserted right away if there is no sign of infection
options.C: IUDs are never recommended after pregnancy termination
options.D: She must wait six weeks for her uterus to shrink

explanation: As long as there's no infection or trauma, an IUD can be placed immediately after the procedure. Saves the patient an extra trip! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h4)

question: What is the best immediate action for the nurse to take after the nebulizer cup runs dry?

options.A: Reassess lung sounds and measure the patient's oxygen saturation
options.B: Immediately start a second dose of medication without waiting
options.C: Disconnect the air flow meter and leave the room quietly
options.D: Instruct the patient to lie flat in bed for one hour

question: Which organ is the main hub for breaking down and metabolizing drugs in the human body?

options.A: Stomach
options.B: Kidneys
options.C: Pancreas
options.D: Liver

explanation: The liver is the powerhouse of drug metabolism! It contains loads of specialized enzymes that transform medications so your body can eventually clear them out. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T4#GNS125_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why do our cells constantly need metabolic processes?

options.A: They completely eliminate the need for intravenous fluids
options.B: They maintain basic life functions and support tissue repair
options.C: They regulate blood pressure by controlling kidney size
options.D: They prevent all forms of bacterial and viral infections

explanation: Cells are tiny powerhouses! They rely on ongoing metabolism to make energy, heal wounds, and keep your body running smoothly every single day. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T010#GNS227_U1_T010_h1)

question: A community midwife in a remote village is treating a woman with severe bleeding after childbirth who needs a blood transfusion. What should she do first?

options.A: Stabilize the patient with available fluids and arrange an immediate emergency referral
options.B: Ask the family members to perform minor surgery in the clinic ward
options.C: Wait until morning before telling anyone about the excessive bleeding
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately to free up the hospital bed

question: Why do family members often feel so distressed when a dying patient stops eating?

options.A: They are worried about the cost of purchasing groceries
options.B: They know that eating is the only cure for their illness
options.C: They believe the hospital kitchen is refusing to cook
options.D: They may view food as a symbol of care and worry the patient is being neglected

explanation: Very true. In our cultures, feeding someone is a deep act of love, so seeing them refuse food can feel heartbreaking to the family. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T17#GNS321_U4_T17_h5)

question: Which finding is specifically linked to Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) rather than HHS?

options.A: Fruity breath odor and Kussmaul respirations
options.B: Extreme dehydration with normal blood pH
options.C: Total absence of any urinary symptoms
options.D: Rapid weight gain due to water retention

explanation: In DKA, the body starts burning fat for fuel because it can't use glucose. This creates acidic ketones, causing a fruity smell on the breath and deep, fast breathing (Kussmaul respirations) as the body tries to blow off the acid. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T14#GNS222_U2_T14_h5)

question: A patient with a history of a traumatic past birth is most likely to experience what during her current labour?

options.B: An increased baseline fetal heart rate
options.C: Heightened anxiety and risk of emotional distress
options.D: Total immunity to contraction pain

explanation: Past bad experiences leave deep emotional footprints. Being aware of this helps you give her that extra dose of reassurance she needs! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T002#GNS226_U4_T002_h3)

question: Why do barrier contraceptives usually have fewer medical restrictions than hormonal birth control pills?

options.A: They require a doctor to insert them every time
options.B: They do not change the body's hormone balance
options.C: They destroy all bacteria present in the vagina
options.D: They are completely 100 percent effective always

question: What is the medical term for a fit?

question: How are Type IV hypersensitivity reactions different from Types I, II, and III?

question: What makes an interdisciplinary team different from a basic multidisciplinary team?

question: What is the primary purpose of checking urine ketones in a patient with severe pregnancy vomiting?

question: Why is it helpful to know that puberty starts at different ages for different teenagers?

question: What is the primary characteristic of a learning disability regarding a person's intelligence?

question: What is the main job of the pudendal nerve in the external genitalia?

question: Which component must be identical in both generic and brand name drugs?

question: Why do nurses stick around and monitor a patient for about 30 minutes after certain shots or vaccines?

question: Why are immediate drug reactions so dangerous?

options.D: They never respond to emergency drugs

question: Why is it so crucial that a patient stays completely still during a spine CT scan?

question: What is the main rule for any food or drink included in a fluid diet?

question: What is the main use of the Nigerian National Formulary?

question: Why is keeping things confidential so vital when caring for teenagers?

question: What is the primary goal of discipline in nursing management?

question: Where should you place defibrillator pads on a patient with an implanted pacemaker?

question: What is the primary purpose of mixing a patient's blood with anti-A serum in the laboratory?

question: Why do patients who receive repeated blood transfusions end up with an overload of iron in their bodies?

options.B: The human body lacks an active physiological mechanism to excrete excess iron

options.D: The liver actively manufactures iron whenever foreign blood is introduced

question: What is the most important thing a nurse checks first during a cholera outbreak?

question: What is the very first step in a standard progressive discipline process?

question: How does a slower kidney filtration rate affect drug safety in older adults?

question: Why is building trust so important during a reproductive health check-in?

question: You are caring for an unconscious patient with a severe brain injury. Which nursing action best prevents aspiration?

question: What is the route of transmission?

question: What is the name of the rounded fatty pad that sits right over the pubic bone?

question: What is the main purpose of the optic chiasm along the visual pathway?

question: Which set of vital signs makes up the famous 'Cushing triad', warning us of severe brainstem compression?

question: Which of these is a classic sign that a patient might have hypothyroidism?

question: Which sign is a classic giveaway of an opioid overdose?

question: What is the main goal of giving blood pressure (antihypertensive) medications?

question: According to Erik Erikson, what is the main psychological challenge teenagers face?

question: How does community health nursing mainly differ from hospital-based nursing care?

question: Which mineral helps a new mother beat fatigue and rebuild iron stores lost during childbirth?

question: What happens to the bladder and urethra during 'urethral hypermobility' when a patient coughs?

question: If an air ring is specially ordered for a patient, what is the correct way to prepare it?

question: What is the primary function of the human skin as a body system?

explanation: Exactly right! It all usually comes down to diet—eating freshwater crabs or crayfish that haven't been cooked enough to kill the parasite. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T26#GNS313_U2_T26_h3)

question: Why should your clinic keep a duplicate copy of every referral form you write?

options.A: To replace client health records permanently with blank sheets
options.B: To prove to the government that the clinic is understaffed
options.C: To track which clients have been sent out and who needs follow-up
options.D: To ensure the client pays a fine if they lose the original paper

explanation: Keeping a duplicate helps you keep tabs on pending cases so no client gets lost along the way. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h6)

question: A patient can bear some weight on one leg and needs to move from the bed to a chair. Which transfer method is best?

options.A: Slide board transfer
options.B: Mechanical lift
options.C: Pivot transfer
options.D: Prone positioning

explanation: A pivot transfer is designed specifically for patients who have enough strength in at least one leg to support a brief pivot movement. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h2)

question: Why do we quickly set up large-bore IV lines for a woman experiencing heavy postpartum bleeding?

options.A: To make it easier to administer oral painkillers and antibiotics
options.B: To prevent the patient from moving her limbs around too much
options.C: To measure the exact temperature of blood flowing through the veins
options.D: To allow rapid infusion of emergency fluids and blood replacement

explanation: Big veins and wide needles let IV fluids and blood rush in fast to fight off shock when a mother is bleeding out. Every second counts! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T013#GNS226_U1_T013_h6)

question: What is the most important approach for a nurse caring for a patient who has undergone FGM?

options.A: Express immediate shock and pity for the patient's condition
options.B: Question the patient aggressively about who performed the act
options.C: Use a trauma-informed, non-judgmental approach to build trust
options.D: Avoid performing any physical examinations to prevent awkwardness

explanation: Wonderful! Creating a safe, empathetic environment lets the patient open up about their health without feeling judged or ashamed. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T1#GNS225_U6_T1_h6)

question: Which condition is classically associated with a "bird-beak" tapering appearance at the bottom of the esophagus?

options.A: Zenker's diverticulum
options.B: Hiatal hernia
options.C: Gastric ulcer
options.D: Achalasia

question: What simple instruction should a nurse give a patient after they use a corticosteroid inhaler?

options.A: Rinse the mouth thoroughly with water and spit it out
options.B: Eat a small snack immediately to protect the throat lining
options.C: Brush the teeth firmly with a hard-bristled toothbrush
options.D: Drink a full glass of milk to neutralize remaining residue

explanation: Always remind patients to rinse and spit! Getting leftover steroid out of the mouth prevents nasty fungal infections like thrush and throat hoarseness. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T5#GNS223_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the main goal of practicing medical asepsis (clean technique) on the ward?

options.A: To sterilize multi-use equipment between patients
options.B: To destroy all bacterial spores on the patient's skin
options.C: To reduce the number of pathogens and stop their spread
options.D: To create a completely germ-free surgical environment

explanation: You got it! Medical asepsis is all about reducing the number of germs and stopping them from traveling around the ward. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h2)

question: How does following the Nigerian National Formulary help protect you as a nurse?

options.A: It allows them to prescribe any foreign drug without a doctor's order
options.B: It grants them the legal authority to open private retail pharmacies
options.C: It safeguards them from liability by using officially approved treatments
options.D: It exempts them from paying professional licensing renewal fees

explanation: Following approved national guidelines keeps you safe professionally. It shows you practiced according to standard, trusted nursing care! [learn more](GNS215_U1_T5#GNS215_U1_T5_h2)

question: A nurse is caring for a patient with a surgical wound. Which finding suggests the local inflammation is worsening into a serious infection?

options.A: A slight drop in blood pressure after getting out of bed
options.B: Mild itching directly over the healing scar line
options.C: Normal skin color surrounding the closed surgical staples
options.D: Pus drainage and spreading redness around the incision

explanation: Purulent drainage and expanding erythema are classic clinical indicators of worsening infection in a wound. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why must nurses emphasize treating sexual partners when a teenager is diagnosed with a bacterial STI?

options.A: To prevent reinfection of the original patient and control community spread
options.B: To ensure the laboratory technicians have enough test samples
options.C: To fulfill mandatory legal requirements for school attendance
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing antibiotics

question: When giving eye drops, where is the safest spot to place the liquid?

options.A: Directly onto the center of the cornea
options.B: Into the lower conjunctival sac
options.C: Onto the upper eyelid surface
options.D: Into the inner corner tear duct

question: A newly admitted patient is shaking before a scheduled biopsy. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Frustration over wearing a standard hospital gown
options.B: Disappointment with the hospital meal schedule
options.C: Anticipation of pain and uncertainty about the diagnosis
options.D: Annoyance with noisy roommates in the ward

explanation: You're right! Not knowing what the results will be, coupled with the worry of physical pain, is a classic recipe for procedure anxiety. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T11#GNS123_U3_T11_h3)

question: What is another common name for the channels connecting the lateral ventricles to the third ventricle?

options.A: Aqueduct of Sylvius

options.C: Foramen magnum
options.D: Apertures of Luschka

question: During an IV insertion, what lets you know for sure that your needle has successfully entered the vein?

options.A: The infusion bag begins to drip rapidly without any pressure.
options.B: The surrounding skin turns pale and cool to the touch.
options.C: The patient reports a sudden cooling sensation in the arm.
options.D: A flash of blood appears inside the flashback chamber of the device.

explanation: That's right! Seeing that little 'flash' of dark red blood in the chamber is the classic sign that you're in the vein. Beautiful work! [learn more](GNS311_U4_T6#GNS311_U4_T6_h5)
